# Problem 1

## a. Expected value and standard deviation (Binomial)

```{r}
n <- 75
p <- 0.45
expected_value <- n * p
std_dev <- sqrt(n * p * (1 - p))
expected_value
std_dev
```

**Explanation:**  
The expected value is 33.75 cured patients, and the standard deviation is approximately 4.31.

---

## b. Probability distribution of all values (numerical and graphical)

```{r}
x_vals <- 0:n
prob_vals <- dbinom(x_vals, size = n, prob = p)

head(data.frame(Cured = x_vals, Probability = prob_vals), 10)

barplot(prob_vals, names.arg = x_vals, 
        main = "Binomial Distribution", xlab = "Cured Patients", 
        ylab = "Probability", border = NA)
```

**Explanation:**  
The distribution shows the likelihood of different cure counts, based on binomial probabilities.

---

## c. Probability of ≤ 30% effectiveness

```{r}
cutoff <- floor(0.30 * n)
p_leq_30 <- pbinom(cutoff, size = n, prob = p)
p_leq_30
```

**Explanation:**  
There is a ~4% chance the cure rate appears to be 30% or lower, even if it's truly 45%.

---

## d. Simulating 10,000 trials

```{r}
set.seed(123)
sim_trials <- rbinom(10000, n, p)

mean(sim_trials)
sd(sim_trials)

hist(sim_trials, breaks = 30, main = "10,000 Simulated Trials", 
     xlab = "Number of Cured Patients")
```

---

# Problem 2

## a. Expected value and standard deviation (Poisson)

```{r}
lambda <- 600
expected_value_pois <- lambda
std_dev_pois <- sqrt(lambda)
expected_value_pois
std_dev_pois
```

**Explanation:**  
For Poisson, both expected value and variance are λ. Here, mean is 600 and SD is ~24.49.

---

## b. Distribution and grouped probabilities

```{r}
x_vals <- 500:700
probs <- dpois(x_vals, lambda)

plot(x_vals, probs, type = "h", main = "Poisson Distribution", 
     xlab = "Number of Patrons", ylab = "Probability")

group_probs <- sapply(seq(500, 700, by = 100), function(start) {
  sum(dpois(start:(start + 99), lambda))
})
names(group_probs) <- c("500–599", "600–699", "700–799")
group_probs
```
